confirmation.description: Why a confirmation was refused; only with code refused.

reason.description: The host's plain words for why the step failed, shown to the user; only for a failed step. Optional.

retryable.description: Whether the failed step can be tried again. Optional.

ConfirmationRecord.description: What the host will apply, issued and worded by the host; confirmed only by sending its single-use token.

CardAnswer.description: The answer the host applied to a card, as it was sent without its protocol; only with answered. A host may leave out a form's values.

answered.description: Whether the host holds an answer to this card; it holds one at most (see the README's Card answers).

BlockDetails.description: Supporting detail behind a disclosure: closed until the user opens it, so the answer comes first.

id.description: The block's id, unique in its message.

fallback.description: Plain text shown by a client that does not know the type.

summary.description: The words on the closed disclosure.

blocks.description: The supporting detail, shown when the disclosure is open.

body.description: The disclosure's words and what it holds.

answered.description: Whether the host holds an answer to a card nested in this block, named in `answer`. An answer marks the message's own block, so a details block that holds a form or buttons is the one marked (see the README's Card answers).

sources.description: What the reply drew on. `[n]` in its content cites the n-th source. Optional.

ReplyStop.description: Asks the host to stop writing a reply. Sent only under the negotiated `reply-stop` capability.

versionIndex.description: The version of the message the stop is for, numbered as the message's `versionIndex` (1 for a message with one version). A host ignores a stop for a version it is not writing. Optional: without it, the stop is for the version being written when it arrives.

label.description: The host's plain words for the read, shown to the user while it runs, for example "Reading 3 orders…". Optional.
